extracted.intended_audience: merchants, shopkeepers, and arithmetic/accounting students (early modern Italian trade)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and calculation methods for merchants: converting currencies and measures, applying tare/reductions, computing profit/loss percentages, and pricing commodities (cloth, grain, metals, barrels, bundles) as given in a historical merchants' arithmetic manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tara / deductions for wax (cera) and similar goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Regole per l'abattimento (tara) e la determinazione del netto per tipi diversi di cera (es. 'la cera nona', 'la cera vecchia') con percentuali e riduzioni applicate in sequenza.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text lists example reductions: '1 cento oe la cera nona vai duci 2... cento oe la cera veciria vai ouc... varrane 8.987...' and instructs to compute the 'ragione' (accounting reason) per piece, to reduce to net by successive abatements, to 'farai la ragione cognunaper' and to 'recotdate dxl oono fegiogtii nel farcia ragione'. In practice: record gross, apply the specified percentage abatements for the category (double/paired reasons where indicated), and compute net/price accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements / quality adjustments (migliaro) for metals and goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentual adjustments when goods are 'migliaro' (improved/assayed) — e.g., '1 migliaro la lana... ual Duc.7é.d5', 'migliaro od ramo... Duc.96', 'migliaro od piombo... ouc.24' — giving conversion/valuation factors for improved vs base material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed improvement rates to adjust value: apply the specific per-mille or per-cento adjustments for each metal or material (rame, stagno, piombo, lana, etc.). The manual shows how to 'applicarali al migliarorfen^a' and use multiplicative factors when multiple improvements or fractions are combined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting and conversion rules for bundles/packs (groffi, faggi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules to convert between large commercial groupings (groffi, faggi) and smaller units, including multiplicative procedures and abatements: e.g. many examples of 'faggi', 'groffi', 'moltiplica... partendo', and sample conversions like 'multiplicandoli per.2 e partendo in cento' to find counts and net values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stepwise multiplication/division procedures given: break large bundles into quarters or other parts, multiply by conversion factors (e.g. 'moltiplica... p.2... partendo in cento'), apply the stated percent abatements (e.g. 'abattendo per 2 per cento'), and then compute net pieces and values. Several worked examples show how to handle remainders and nested multiplications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting foreign coins/monete to local standard (ducats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle: convert foreign coinage into the local ducat value by stated rates; e.g. 'monete ponantar in relais... le valute come ancona 1020 fi mettano ì regola' and rules for reducing quantities 'alultime monetetebaueraì Duc.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To compare prices across markets, reduce foreign coins to Duc. using the given exchange rates, then perform multiplications/divisions to express amounts in ducats or to reduce to the 'last coin' units. The manual gives examples of reducing 'quantità alultùnemonete' and repeated multiplication to reach the comparable unit. When converting multiple currencies, reduce to one reference coin before comparing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute profit/gain as percent of cost or capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Method to compute guadagno (gain) and perdita (loss) expressed as percent: compare sale price and purchase/capital, express gain as 'per cento' of cost/capitale, and use multiplication to scale to desired units ('moltiplica... via... fa...')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual repeatedly instructs: find difference (sale - cost) = gain; express gain as percentage of cost or capital; to find final amounts or to find capital given a gain, use multiplicative methods (examples: '1 440 faao... per la regola... fuo guadagno amodo pmo', 'multiplica... via... fa...'). Worked numeric examples illustrate computing capital from gain, or gain from capital, using repeated multiplication/division by 100 and by the percent factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limiting allowable profits by regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices about legal/regulatory limits on profits: 'Regula innclliédicum limitatfonc lucri 7 Danni-orticuluo octauu' and instructions to 'limitare li guadagni' in certain forms of trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When local rules cap allowable profit, adjust calculations to conform: compute what the sale/gain would be, then reduce to the regulated maximum by computing the permitted percent and re-evaluating the price so the merchant does not exceed the legal gain. The text warns that artificially limiting allowable gain can prevent speculation and may change capital recovery calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures and volume conversions for liquids and containers (barile, botte, petto)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules to convert between container measures (barile, botte, 'il barile', 'la botte', 'il petitto') and to compute price per container unit: e.g., 'la foma dd nino... el barile ne tiene.20', 'a tanto el petitto.£ a tanto el barile.£ a tanto la botte' and subsequent reduction procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the stated container capacities and relations (how many 'piccoli' fit a 'barile', etc.), then reduce or multiply to express quantities in the desired container unit. When pricing by container, apply reductions proportional to the container filling, and reduce to standard measures (foldi, piedi) as the manual demonstrates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land area and linear measure conversions (tauola del terreno)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables and rules for land measures: 'la tauola del terreno ual 12... Ioga per ogni verfo... piedi', 'la minima del terreno... opera reducendo al ultime' and how to convert between 'tauole', 'piedi', 'foldo' etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the tabulated equivalences: convert lengths/areas via the given unit relations (piedi per tauola, folds per measure). To compute area-based prices, reduce the land measure to the standard table unit and apply the price per table or per piede as shown, including any reductions for submultiples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling measures sold 'colme' (full measures) and partial measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on measures 'colme'—full measures—versus partial measures: 'le mefure colme fe coftuma mercare tutte' and the list of common measured goods (bocali, fogliette, banli, forme, lire, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When goods are sold by full measure, use the 'colma' standard (fill-to-top) as reference; for partial or different containers, convert to the colma-equivalent before pricing. The manual lists which goods customarily use colma measures and shows how to transform arbitrary containers into equivalent colme for consistent pricing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing finished textiles: 'bacio', 'panno' and finishing costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for pricing cloth/pan n o based on finishing and quality indicators like 'bacio del panno', 'bagnatura e cinatura', with percentage adjustments for finishing steps and quality ('il b2acio del panno ual S:.5i.dx uara bañda...')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for finishing operations by adding/removing fixed percentages corresponding to processes (washing, finishing, hemming). The manual demonstrates computing final price by starting with base price, adding finishing percent (or subtracting for defects), and then reducing to unit measures (per 'bacio' or per 'canna').

rubrics_metrics.name: Using repeated multiplication and fractional partitioning to scale prices and counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructional pattern present throughout: perform repeated multiplication ('moltiplica... via... fa...') and partition into parts/quarters when scaling up or down quantities and prices (e.g., splitting bundles into quarters, multiplying by conversion factors, then reducing by percent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To scale a rate or unit price for N items, repeatedly multiply by N or by 100 then divide/multiply as necessary to get percent-based results. When quantities are partitioned (quarters, thirds), compute unit equivalents by dividing and then recombining with multipliers. Numerous worked examples illustrate the technique for both piece counts and monetary computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for comparing market prices and deciding whether sale yields profit
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure: reduce local and foreign prices to a common unit (moneta/ducat), compute effective gain or loss after abatements/fees, and decide whether to sell or hold ('fe coftuma inercare... confrontare i mercati e vedere il guadagno e la pdita')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare purchase price (in standardized units) with expected sale price (after conversion and abatements). Determine gain percent and whether it justifies selling; consider transport costs, duties, and regulated profit limits. The manual recommends calculating capital recovery and net gain in several scenarios to decide the best commercial action; examples detail when to sell immediately versus hold for price movement.
